rules.title: Maximum Tenant Screening Fee (Annual State Cap)
rules.requirement: California landlords may charge a prospective tenant a screening/application fee only up to an annually-adjusted statutory cap; for 2026 the maximum is $68.96. The fee may only cover the cost of obtaining things like a consumer credit report and processing the application, unused portions must be refunded, and the fee cannot be charged if no unit is actually available or (unless using a first-qualified-applicant policy) to applicants not ultimately selected.
rules.exemptions: No fee may be charged if no rental unit is actually available. Landlord must refund the fee to any applicant not selected, unless using a policy of reviewing applications in order received, giving the unit to the first qualified applicant, and not charging a fee to applicants not considered.
rules.interaction: Berkeley Municipal Code § 13.78.010 requires local landlords to additionally disclose this state fee cap and the tenant's screening fee rights before collecting the fee.
rules.quoted_span: The maximum tenant screening fee for 2026 is $68.96

rules.title: Mandatory Use of Reusable Tenant Screening Reports
rules.requirement: If a prospective tenant furnishes the landlord with a reusable (portable) tenant screening report, the landlord must use that report rather than requiring the applicant to pay for a new one.
rules.quoted_span: If the tenant provides a reusable screening report, the landlord must use it.

rules.title: Tenant Screening Fee Rights Disclosure Requirement
rules.requirement: Before or when charging a fee to purchase a consumer credit report or otherwise process a rental application, a Berkeley owner or agent must provide a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap under state law, either in the rental application itself or in a separate disclosure given before the fee is collected.
rules.interaction: Cross-references the fee cap set by California Civil Code Section 1950.6(b).

rules.title: Ban on Non-Refundable Fees for Existing Tenancy Renewals
rules.requirement: A Berkeley owner or agent cannot charge an existing tenant any non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy, including a fee tied to a roommate leaving, or to adding or replacing a roommate in an existing household.
rules.interaction: Per Berkeley Municipal Code § 13.78.018, this applies to all residential rental agreements regardless of contrary lease language, and conflicting lease provisions are unenforceable.
rules.quoted_span: cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household
